paragraphs: Compositional communication represents complicated ideas by combining simpler pieces. CELEBI investigates how artificial agents can learn this property through a communication game: a sender produces discrete symbols, and a receiver uses them to reconstruct information. The framework combines pressures to keep messages compact, expressive, and efficient, rather than relying on reconstruction alone to produce structured language.

Three mechanisms shape the learned messages. Progressive Decoding asks the receiver for a partial reconstruction after every symbol, encouraging useful intermediate interpretation. Final-State Imitation has successive generations imitate reconstructed outcomes instead of copying messages, tightening the communication bottleneck. Pairwise Distance Maximization encourages messages to remain distinct, with a formal connection to maximizing entropy.

On Shapes3D and MPI3D, CELEBI improves message efficiency and compositionality while outperforming earlier discrete communication frameworks in reconstruction accuracy and topographic similarity. These results provide theoretical and experimental support for the idea that simplicity-oriented learning pressures can encourage structured, generalizable communication. The evidence concerns learned communication protocols in the studied settings.
neurips-2025-a-compressive-expressive-co.tldr: CELEBI combines three communication pressures to help artificial agents learn compact, expressive, and more compositional messages.

paragraphs: DreamLight addresses the problem of placing a subject into a new background while making the lighting and color feel consistent. It supports both backgrounds supplied as images and backgrounds generated from text prompts. The central challenge is to create natural interactions between foreground and background lighting while preserving the subject’s appearance.

The method puts its inputs into a shared format and draws on a pretrained diffusion model’s learned visual knowledge. Its Position-Guided Light Adapter gathers directional lighting information from the background into light query embeddings. Direction-sensitive masked attention then uses that information to modify the foreground, giving background illumination a spatially informed role in the relighting process.

A separate post-processing component, the Spectral Foreground Fixer, adaptively reorganizes frequency components from the subject and relighted background to improve foreground consistency. Extensive comparisons and a user study support the reported relighting performance. Together, the components address two linked goals: making the subject fit the new lighting and keeping its visual appearance consistent through the transformation.
neurips-2025-dreamlight-towards-harmonio.tldr: DreamLight uses directional lighting guidance and frequency-based post-processing to harmonize subjects with image- or text-specified backgrounds.

paragraphs: Sequential reasoning requires choosing what to do next at each stage of a problem. A manually specified menu of actions can be difficult to scale, while an unrestricted menu can make search prohibitively expensive. DynaAct addresses this tension by automatically constructing a compact set of candidate actions suited to the current reasoning state.

The framework first uses large language models to extract general action sketches from a corpus of varied, complex reasoning problems. These sketches provide an approximation to the complete action space. It then scores candidate sets using a submodular function that combines usefulness for the current state with diversity, and applies a greedy selection algorithm.

This design makes action selection itself part of the reasoning process: the system seeks relevant options without filling its candidate set with similar alternatives. Experiments on six standard benchmarks report significant overall performance improvements while preserving efficient inference without substantial additional latency. The findings support compact, dynamically selected action spaces as a practical way to improve sequential problem solving.
neurips-2025-dynaact-large-language-mode.tldr: DynaAct improves sequential reasoning by dynamically selecting compact action sets that balance immediate usefulness with diversity.

paragraphs: Cross-modal retrieval connects information across formats, such as finding images that match text. Hash-based methods make this search efficient, but their compact representations can fail to capture shared meaning across modalities. AHLR targets this semantic mismatch, particularly when important information is missed or feature channels receive inappropriate weight during learning.

The method combines dynamic masking with an auxiliary hash layer. During training, dynamic masking selects and weights key information in images and text to improve feature matching. The auxiliary layer adaptively balances feature weights across channels, addressing uneven channel contributions. A contrastive loss further shapes the resulting hash codes so they better distinguish matching information from alternatives.

Experiments on NUS-WIDE, MIRFlickr-25K, and MS-COCO show that AHLR outperforms several existing algorithms. The stated findings suggest that retrieval quality benefits from jointly improving what information is retained, how channels contribute, and how the final codes are separated. The contribution is therefore a coordinated training approach for more informative cross-modal hash representations.
neurips-2025-dynamic-masking-and-auxilia.tldr: AHLR improves image–text hash retrieval by dynamically emphasizing useful information, balancing feature channels, and learning more discriminative codes.

paragraphs: Automatically discovering statistical relationships creates a second problem: deciding which ones deserve attention. This paper focuses on assessing correlations by comparing observed values with what a language model would expect. A relationship that differs from the model’s expectations can be ranked as more surprising and potentially worth further exploration.

The proposed Logit-based Calibrated Prior converts a model’s raw output scores into a continuous probability distribution over possible correlation values. This provides an expectation with uncertainty, rather than only a positive-or-negative prediction. The distribution acts as a reference for assessing observations, connecting knowledge encoded in model weights to hypothesis prioritization.

On 2,096 real-world variable pairs, the method achieves 78.8% sign accuracy and a mean absolute error of 0.26. Its 95% credible intervals cover 89.2% of observed values. It also improves binary prediction over a fine-tuned RoBERTa classifier and achieves higher precision in top-ranked hypotheses. Generalization to correlations absent from pretraining supports context-sensitive reasoning as an explanation beyond memorization.
neurips-2025-exploiting-llms-for-automat.tldr: A calibrated distribution derived from LLM logits helps rank observed correlations by how surprising they are relative to model expectations.

paragraphs: Federated learning lets distributed devices contribute to shared model training while keeping their data local. Differences in hardware can make this process slow because resource-limited clients delay aggregation. FedEL aims to improve training speed while preserving accuracy and keeping slower devices involved in a coordinated learning process.

Its main mechanism is a sliding training window that determines which portion of the model a client trains. Within a coordinated runtime budget, FedEL dynamically selects important tensors from that portion. Moving the window supports progressive, balanced training across clients. A separate adjustment module reconciles local and global tensor importance to reduce biases associated with differences in client data.

Experiments report up to a 3.87-fold improvement in time-to-accuracy over the evaluated baselines, while matching or exceeding their final test accuracy. This is a reported maximum improvement, rather than a uniform gain for every setting. The results support adapting the amount and location of training work to device capabilities while coordinating contributions across the model.
neurips-2025-fedel-federated-elastic-lea.tldr: FedEL coordinates selective model training across unequal devices, reporting up to 3.87× better time-to-accuracy while preserving final accuracy.

paragraphs: Infinite-width analyses often approximate neural network variables with Gaussian distributions. Attention has resisted that treatment under ordinary architectural choices, with earlier Gaussian descriptions requiring special scaling or infinitely many attention heads. This paper uses Tensor Programs to characterize the limiting distribution inside a single attention layer under standard inverse-square-root scaling.

The derived distribution is fundamentally non-Gaussian overall, but its structure is more specific than that label alone suggests. Conditional on the random similarity scores used by attention, the distribution is Gaussian. The randomness in those scores creates a hierarchy that changes the unconditional distribution. This distinction explains why a simple Gaussian approximation misses part of attention’s behavior.

Numerical experiments support the theoretical predictions and show that the description is useful at finite width and with finitely many heads. The result establishes an exact limiting law for the studied single layer without the special regimes previously needed. It also offers groundwork for a broader theory of deep Transformers, rather than already providing that complete theory.
neurips-2025-infinite-width-limit-of-a-s.tldr: A single attention layer has a non-Gaussian infinite-width limit under standard scaling, although it is Gaussian conditional on random similarity scores.

paragraphs: Animals explore without needing an externally assigned task or reward. This paper investigates how an artificial agent’s internal learning objective can produce comparable autonomy and help explain natural behavior. It addresses shortcomings in existing model-based exploration methods, which the authors describe as having inconsistent exploration and failing to converge to an exploratory policy.

The proposed drive, 3M-Progress, tracks divergence between a continually updated world model and a fixed prior learned from an ecological niche. This relationship supplies the agent’s intrinsic goal. The embodied agent is optimized through self-supervision without behavioral or neural training data, allowing its resulting activity to be compared with independently recorded biological observations.

The authors report that the agents capture explainable variance in behavioral patterns and whole-brain neural-glial dynamics from autonomously behaving larval zebrafish. They present this as, to their knowledge, the first autonomous embodied agent predicting brain data through such intrinsic-goal optimization alone. The findings connect a computational exploration objective with naturalistic behavior and population-level neural-glial activity.
neurips-2025-intrinsic-goals-for-autonom.tldr: 3M-Progress links an intrinsic exploration objective to zebrafish-like behavior and brain dynamics without training on behavioral or neural recordings.

paragraphs: Inverse problems involve recovering an underlying signal from a degraded observation. Diffusion models can generate possible reconstructions, but the abstract identifies a trade-off between two approaches. Zero-shot methods accommodate arbitrary linear degradations while relying on accuracy-reducing approximations; supervised methods model the posterior correctly but lack adaptation to the degradation at test time.

InvFusion addresses this trade-off by incorporating the degradation operator directly into the diffusion denoiser. The resulting architecture is trained while remaining aware of how an observation was degraded. This gives the reconstruction model direct access to the transformation it must account for, aiming to combine supervised reconstruction quality with the flexibility associated with zero-shot methods.

Experiments on FFHQ and ImageNet report state-of-the-art performance against general-purpose posterior samplers, including degradation-aware zero-shot methods and blind trained methods. The authors also demonstrate the architecture as a minimum-mean-square-error predictor and a neural posterior principal-component estimator. These additional uses show that its degradation-aware design supports more than posterior sampling alone.
neurips-2025-invfusion-bridging-supervis.tldr: InvFusion builds the degradation operator into a trained diffusion denoiser to combine reconstruction quality with degradation-aware flexibility.

paragraphs: Agent-based models describe complex systems through many individuals following local, often random rules. Their collective behavior emerges from those interactions. However, hand-designed rules are generally not differentiable, which makes gradient-based optimization and integration with real-world data difficult. This paper proposes learning a differentiable replacement from data generated by an agent-based model.

The framework combines two modeling tools with complementary roles. Diffusion models represent randomness in individual behavior, while graph neural networks represent interactions between agents. Crucially, the learned surrogate predicts individual behavior rather than directly approximating only system-wide outputs. That choice preserves the decentralized route through which local decisions produce larger-scale patterns.

The authors evaluate the method on Schelling’s segregation model and a Predator-Prey ecosystem. In these examples, it reproduces individual-level patterns and forecasts emergent dynamics beyond training. Although the framework is proposed for arbitrary agent-based models, the reported validation concerns these two cases. The results demonstrate the potential of learning local stochastic behavior while retaining the bottom-up organization of the original simulation.
neurips-2025-learning-individual-behavio.tldr: Graph diffusion networks learn individual agent behavior from simulation data while preserving the local interactions that produce emergent dynamics.

paragraphs: In heterophilous graphs, connected nodes often differ from one another, making immediate neighbors potentially difficult sources of predictive information. A deeper graph neural network can inspect more distant neighborhoods, where similar nodes may become accessible. Yet increasing depth can also degrade performance, so a larger information-gathering scope does not automatically translate into better predictions.

The paper studies this tension theoretically and empirically. It finds that changing depth shifts generalization preferences across nodes with different levels of homophily. Consequently, shallow and deep versions of a network can have different patterns of strengths across nodes. This provides a reason to consider their scopes jointly rather than treating depth as a uniformly beneficial choice.

Based on that analysis, Moscat combines scope experts at test time to improve deeper networks’ generalization while retaining their expressivity. Experiments show significant accuracy improvements across a wide range of datasets and compatibility with various graph neural network architectures. The findings support using the complementary generalization patterns of shallow and deep variants.
neurips-2025-mixture-of-scope-experts-at.tldr: Moscat improves deeper graph networks by combining experts with different neighborhood scopes at test time.

paragraphs: Generating audio for video requires both realistic sound and a meaningful match between what is heard and what is seen. MGAudio addresses these objectives through a flow-based generation framework with a dedicated training objective that lets the generative model guide itself. Its central design connects audiovisual conditioning with feature alignment.

The architecture contains a scalable Transformer denoiser and an audiovisual encoder with two responsibilities. The encoder supplies information that conditions audio generation, and it also acts as a feature aligner to improve the generated result. A model-guided objective reinforces cross-modal coherence and audio realism, making the guidance mechanism part of the framework’s training design.

On VGGSound, MGAudio reports state-of-the-art performance, including an FAD of 0.40 and improvements over the best evaluated classifier-free guidance baselines. It also outperforms existing methods across FD, IS, and alignment metrics, and generalizes well to UnAV-100. These findings support the combined use of self-guidance and dual-role audiovisual alignment for high-quality video-conditioned audio.
neurips-2025-model-guided-dual-role-alig.tldr: MGAudio combines model self-guidance with an audiovisual encoder that both conditions and aligns generated sound, improving realism and video–audio coherence.

paragraphs: MoGe-2 reconstructs a scene’s three-dimensional point map from a single image, with the added goal of recovering metric scale. Its predecessor, MoGe, predicts affine-invariant point maps whose scale is unknown. The new work explores how to add real-scale geometry prediction while preserving the accurate relative geometry supported by that representation.

The paper also identifies training-data quality as a cause of lost detail. Noise and errors in real data can blur fine structures in predicted geometry. To address this, the authors introduce a refinement process that filters and completes real data using sharp synthetic labels. This improves the granularity of reconstruction while maintaining overall geometric accuracy.

After training on a large mixture of datasets, MoGe-2 is evaluated for relative geometry, metric scale, and fine detail. The authors report superior performance across these capabilities and describe their simultaneous achievement as a distinction from previous methods. The contribution combines an extension of the geometric representation’s capabilities with a targeted improvement to the supervision used for learning.
neurips-2025-moge-2-accurate-monocular-g.tldr: MoGe-2 estimates metric-scale 3D geometry from one image while preserving relative accuracy and improving detail through refined training data.

paragraphs: Online video anomaly detection must identify unusual behavior as video arrives. This creates different computational and timing demands from analyzing a complete recording. MoniTor introduces a training-free approach that supplies streaming input to pretrained vision-language models and uses memory to help interpret the current moment in the context of recent events.

A prediction mechanism inspired by Long Short-Term Memory networks incorporates past states and earlier predictions. This helps the model account for temporal dependencies instead of treating the current frame in isolation. A scoring queue stores recent anomaly scores, while an anomaly prior provides additional guidance for language models distinguishing normal and abnormal behavior over time.

The method is evaluated on UCF-Crime and XD-Violence, which contain surveillance and other real-world scenarios. The authors report that MoniTor outperforms state-of-the-art methods and remains competitive with weakly supervised approaches without additional training. The results support combining pretrained model capabilities with explicit temporal memory and score-based guidance for online anomaly assessment.
neurips-2025-monitor-exploiting-large-la.tldr: MoniTor uses pretrained models, temporal memory, and a recent-score queue to detect video anomalies online without additional training.

paragraphs: This position paper argues that sound AI policy needs mechanisms for forming scientific consensus alongside rigorous evidence. The authors distinguish producing evidence, synthesizing existing evidence, and establishing a shared scientific position. They identify an absence of mechanisms for the third activity, even as structures for the first two already exist or are beginning to develop.

Their proposal is for NeurIPS to help fill this institutional gap. They argue that its strengths and the lack of compelling alternatives make it the best available choice. As a practical starting point, they recommend initial pilots informed by lessons from the IPCC’s role in building scientific consensus relevant to climate policy.

The paper also addresses anticipated objections: that disagreement among AI researchers makes consensus unattainable, and that policy engagement falls outside NeurIPS’s responsibilities. Its contribution is an institutional argument and a proposed direction for action, rather than an experimental demonstration. The intended outcome is a stronger shared scientific foundation for policies that better realize AI’s benefits.
neurips-2025-neurips-should-lead-scienti.tldr: This position paper argues that NeurIPS should pilot mechanisms for scientific consensus on AI policy, drawing lessons from the IPCC.

paragraphs: Finding densely connected parts of a directed graph supports tasks such as clustering and community detection. This paper develops approximation algorithms for settings where graphs are too large for conventional processing. It studies both massively parallel computation, where machines coordinate their work, and semi-streaming, where edges are processed with restricted memory.

The parallel algorithm achieves a (2 + ε)-approximation in roughly the square root of log n rounds, up to suppressed logarithmic factors, with sublinear memory per machine. The streaming algorithm obtains an O(log n)-approximation in one deterministic pass. The authors identify it as the first deterministic single-pass semi-streaming algorithm for this problem in both directed and undirected graphs.

The streaming approach also supports insertion-only updates with O(log² n) worst-case update time and sublinear memory. Empirically, its approximation on temporal datasets matches that of a compared multipass algorithm, exceeding what its worst-case guarantee alone suggests. The parallel method also requires fewer rounds than prior work. These results combine formal resource guarantees with evidence of stronger practical behavior.
neurips-2025-new-parallel-and-streaming-.tldr: New parallel and deterministic single-pass algorithms approximate directed densest subgraphs with improved computation and memory guarantees.

paragraphs: OpenWorldSAM extends SAM2 so that language can specify what an image segmentation model should identify. The challenge is to connect textual meaning with precise image regions, including objects from unseen categories. The framework accepts both category names and sentence-level descriptions, giving different segmentation tasks a shared language-based interface.

It integrates multimodal embeddings from a lightweight vision-language model while freezing the pretrained components of both that model and SAM2. Only 4.5 million parameters are trained on COCO-stuff. To distinguish multiple instances, the framework adds positional tie-breaker embeddings and cross-attention layers, improving the spatial information available when grounding a prompt in an image.

Experiments report state-of-the-art results across open-vocabulary semantic, instance, and panoptic segmentation benchmarks. The authors also report strong zero-shot performance on unseen categories and concepts without additional training. These findings suggest that a relatively small trainable extension can connect pretrained language–vision representations with SAM2’s segmentation capabilities while supporting both broad categories and more descriptive prompts.
neurips-2025-openworldsam-extending-sam2.tldr: OpenWorldSAM adds flexible language prompting and instance awareness to frozen SAM2 and vision-language components using 4.5 million trainable parameters.

paragraphs: Reconstructing a physical field from a few measurements depends on both the reconstruction method and where the sensors are placed. PhySense treats these as coupled decisions. Its motivation is that improving reconstruction alone leaves useful information untapped when sensor locations are held outside the optimization process.

The framework has two stages. First, a flow-based generative model uses cross-attention to combine sparse observations adaptively and reconstruct the field. Second, feedback from reconstruction guides sensor placement through projected gradient descent. The projection allows the placement optimization to respect spatial constraints, connecting the search for informative measurements with the locations that are permitted.

The authors prove that the objectives of both stages agree with classical variance-minimization principles. Experiments across three challenging benchmarks, including a three-dimensional geometry dataset, report state-of-the-art sensing accuracy and informative placements that had not previously been considered. The findings support a coordinated approach in which reconstruction quality helps determine where observations should be collected, rather than treating sensor arrangement as a separate preliminary choice.
neurips-2025-physense-sensor-placement-o.tldr: PhySense links physical-field reconstruction with spatially constrained sensor placement to improve what sparse measurements can reveal.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks can perform poorly when test data differ from training data. One response is to identify a subgraph whose relationship with the target remains stable across distributions. This paper argues that directly selecting such edges is error-prone because misleading edges can still correlate strongly with the target during training.

PrunE approaches the problem by removing spurious edges. The goal is to preserve the invariant subgraph more comprehensively through selective deletion. Two regularization terms guide that process: a graph-size constraint excludes uninformative spurious edges, and an ε-probability alignment term further suppresses spurious edges. These mechanisms focus learning on reducing misleading graph structure.

The authors support the approach with theoretical analysis and extensive experiments, reporting significantly better out-of-distribution performance than previous state-of-the-art methods. The stated results make pruning an alternative route to recovering stable predictive structure. The key idea is that deciding which connections to discard can help preserve useful structure that a direct selection procedure might otherwise miss.
neurips-2025-pruning-spurious-subgraphs-.tldr: PrunE improves graph generalization under distribution shifts by pruning spurious edges to preserve stable predictive structure.

paragraphs: Validating a vehicle’s motion plan requires understanding both the driving situation and the planner’s decision. Techniques borrowed from image classification face complex contextual inputs and multiple possible plans for a situation. Meanwhile, evaluating predicted trajectories without feedback does not fully reflect closed-loop planning, where decisions affect what happens next.

REDOUBT introduces a dual validation mechanism that checks input distributions alongside output uncertainty. It examines combinations of familiar or unfamiliar scenarios and certain or uncertain decisions, exposing unsafe modes that earlier approaches overlooked. One module detects out-of-distribution inputs through latent flow matching; another uses an energy-based approach to estimate uncertainty in planning decisions.

Experiments show that both modules outperform existing approaches under open-loop and closed-loop evaluation. The contribution is a coordinated framework for assessing complementary signals of planning safety, with methods tailored to motion planning’s contextual structure. The findings support examining how scenario familiarity and decision uncertainty interact, rather than assuming that either signal alone adequately characterizes the evaluated unsafe behavior.
neurips-2025-redoubt-duo-safety-validati.tldr: REDOUBT jointly assesses scenario distribution and planning uncertainty to identify unsafe autonomous-driving decisions.

paragraphs: Distributional regression estimates a predictive distribution rather than only a single mean value. This paper studies how accurately nonparametric methods can perform that task. Its main contribution is a set of upper bounds on estimation risk, providing theoretical control over errors for different families of constrained distributional estimators.

For convex constraints, the authors establish general bounds using the continuous ranked probability score and worst-case mean squared error across the domain. They then apply these results to isotonic and trend-filtering distributional regression. The resulting convergence rates are consistent with those for mean estimation, connecting the statistical behavior of these distribution-estimation methods with that of their mean-estimation counterparts.

The analysis also extends to non-convex constraints through another general upper bound, with neural-network estimators as a specific application. Experiments on simulated and real data support the theoretical contributions and their practical effectiveness. Together, the results provide a framework for understanding estimation error across several distributional regression approaches, while retaining the distinction between their constraint structures.
neurips-2025-risk-bounds-for-distributio.tldr: The paper derives risk bounds for constrained distributional regression, including isotonic, trend-filtering, and neural-network estimators.

paragraphs: Template-based molecular generation builds compounds using predefined reaction templates and building blocks, connecting molecule design with synthesis routes. This paper addresses three challenges for template-based GFlowNets: reducing synthesis cost, handling large building-block libraries, and making productive use of small fragment collections. The approach considers how molecules can be constructed as part of generation itself.

Recursive Cost Guidance uses auxiliary machine learning models to approximate synthesis cost and viability within a backward-policy framework. These estimates steer generation toward less expensive synthesis pathways. An Exploitation Penalty complements that guidance by balancing exploration and exploitation, helping the method pursue favorable routes while retaining molecular diversity.

For smaller libraries, a Dynamic Library mechanism reuses intermediate states with high rewards to build complete synthesis trees. The authors report state-of-the-art template-based generation results, with improvements in cost efficiency, diversity, and molecular quality, especially when cost guidance is combined with the penalty. The findings show the value of coordinating pathway cost, search behavior, and reuse of promising intermediates.
neurips-2025-scalable-and-cost-efficient.tldr: Cost guidance, exploration control, and reusable intermediates improve template-based molecular generation across building-block library sizes.

paragraphs: Recursive synthetic training uses outputs from one model generation to train later generations. Errors can accumulate through this process, producing the progressive decline called model collapse. This paper develops a theoretical account of those dynamics and shows exponential error growth in its framework unless sufficient real data mitigate the accumulation.

To address settings where real data are scarce, the authors introduce self-verification: models filter their own generated outputs using internal confidence scores. The mechanism does not require external validation. Its purpose is to change which synthetic examples enter subsequent training, making selection within the recursive process central to controlling error.

The analysis derives finite-sample error bounds showing that self-verification alone can prevent collapse, including in fully synthetic training regimes. The framework also extends to language models and characterizes conditions under which recursive training stays stable without performance degradation. This is a conditional theoretical result: it establishes circumstances in which internal verification is sufficient, rather than asserting that any confidence-based filter will stabilize every recursive training process.
neurips-2025-self-verification-provably-.tldr: The paper derives conditions under which confidence-based self-verification prevents model collapse even when recursive training uses only synthetic data.

paragraphs: Spiking neural networks offer potential energy efficiency through event-driven computation, but they struggle with visual tasks involving long sequences. This paper introduces the Spatio-Temporal Effective Receptive Field, or ST-ERF, to examine how information across space and time influences these networks. It applies the tool to several Transformer-based spiking architectures.

The analysis finds difficulty establishing a robust global spatiotemporal receptive field, limiting visual feature modeling. To address this, the authors propose two channel-mixing architectures: MLPixer and the splash-and-reconstruct block. Both expand the effective spatial reach across all timesteps early in the network, targeting the specific information-coverage weakness revealed by ST-ERF.

Experiments on Meta-SDT variants and on object detection and semantic segmentation support the proposed improvements. The contribution therefore combines a diagnostic method with architectural changes motivated by its findings. The authors also suggest that ST-ERF could guide the design of spiking networks for a broader range of tasks; that broader applicability is presented as a prospect beyond the demonstrated evaluations.
neurips-2025-unveiling-the-spatial-tempo.tldr: ST-ERF reveals limited global information coverage in Transformer-based spiking networks and motivates two channel mixers that improve visual modeling.

paragraphs: Giving a language model more computation during inference can improve reasoning, but that computation can be spent in different ways. Repeated sampling produces many candidate answers, benefiting from the model’s response diversity. However, it does not use external feedback to refine those candidates, even when such feedback is available in tasks such as coding.

Adaptive Branching Monte Carlo Tree Search, or AB-MCTS, combines generating alternatives with revisiting existing responses. At each point in its search tree, it dynamically chooses whether to expand outward with new candidates or pursue further refinement of an existing one. External feedback helps guide that choice, connecting exploration with multi-turn improvement.

The authors evaluate the framework on complex coding and engineering tasks using frontier models. AB-MCTS outperforms both repeated sampling and standard MCTS in these experiments. The findings support allocating inference-time computation between diverse attempts and feedback-driven refinement, rather than relying on either behavior alone. The demonstrated advantage concerns the evaluated tasks, where external feedback can inform the search.
neurips-2025-wider-or-deeper-scaling-llm.tldr: AB-MCTS uses external feedback to choose between generating new answers and refining existing ones, improving evaluated coding and engineering performance.
